Now that we've finally gotten rid of the non-atomic MST users leftover in
the kernel
column2: we can finally get rid of all of the legacy payload code we

column1: have and move as much as possible into the MST atomic state structs. The
main purpose of this is to make the MST code a lot less confusing to work
on
column2: as there's a lot of duplicated logic that doesn't really need to be

column1: here. As well
column2: this should make introducing features like fallback link

column1: retraining and DSC support far easier.
Since the old payload code was pretty gnarly and there's a Lot of changes
here
column2: I expect this might be a bit difficult to review. So to make things

column1: as easy as possible for reviewers
column2: I'll sum up how both the old and new

column1: code worked here (it took me a while to figure this out too!).
The old MST code basically worked by maintaining two different payload
tables - proposed_vcpis
column2: and payloads. proposed_vcpis would hold the

column1: modified payload we wanted to push to the topology
column2: while payloads held the

column1: payload table that was currently programmed in hardware. Modifications to
proposed_vcpis would be handled through drm_dp_allocate_vcpi()
drm_dp_mst_deallocate_vcpi()
column2: and drm_dp_mst_reset_vcpi_slots(). Then

column1: would be pushed via drm_dp_mst_update_payload_step1() and
drm_dp_mst_update_payload_step2().
Furthermore
column2: it's important to note how adding and removing VC payloads

column1: actually worked with drm_dp_mst_update_payload_step1(). When a VC payload
is removed from the VC table
column2: all VC payloads which come after the removed

column1: VC payload's slots must have their time slots shifted towards the start of
the table. The old code handles this by looping through the entire payload
table and recomputing the start slot for every payload in the topology from
scratch. While very much overkill
column2: this ends up doing the right thing

column1: because we always order the VCPIs for payloads from first to last starting
timeslot.
It's important to also note that drm_dp_mst_update_payload_step2() isn't
actually limited to updating a single payload - the driver can use it to
queue up multiple payload changes so that as many of them can be sent as
possible before waiting for the ACT. This is -technically- not against
spec
column2: but as Wayne Lin has pointed out it's not consistently implemented

column1: correctly in hubs - so it might as well be.
drm_dp_mst_update_payload_step2() is pretty self explanatory and basically
the same between the old and new code
column2: save for the fact we don't have a

column1: second step for deleting payloads anymore -and thus rename it to
drm_dp_mst_add_payload_step2().
The new payload code stores all of the current payload info within the MST
atomic state and computes as much of the state as possible ahead of time.
This has the one exception of the starting timeslots for payloads
column2: which

column1: can't be determined at atomic check time since the starting time slots will
vary depending on what order CRTCs are enabled in the atomic state - which
varies from driver to driver. These are still stored in the atomic MST
state
column2: but are only copied from the old MST state during atomic commit

column1: time. Likewise
column2: this is when new start slots are determined.

column1: Adding/removing payloads now works much more closely to how things are
described in the spec. When we delete a payload
column2: we loop through the

column1: current list of payloads and update the start slots for any payloads whose
time slots came after the payload we just deleted. Determining the starting
time slots for new payloads being added is done by simply keeping track of
where the end of the VC table is in
drm_dp_mst_topology_mgr->next_start_slot. Additionally
column2: it's worth noting

column1: that we no longer have a single update_payload() function. Instead
column2: we now

column1: have drm_dp_mst_add_payload_step1|2() and drm_dp_mst_remove_payload(). As
such
column2: it's now left it up to the driver to figure out when to add or remove

column1: payloads. The driver already knows when it's disabling/enabling CRTCs
column2: so

column1: it also already knows when payloads should be added or removed.
Changes since v1:
* Refactor around all of the completely dead code changes that are
happening in amdgpu for some reason when they really shouldn't even be
there in the first place… :\
* Remove mention of sending one ACT per series of payload updates. As Wayne
Lin pointed out
column2: there are apparently hubs on the market that don't work

column1: correctly with this scheme and require a separate ACT per payload update.
* Fix accidental drop of mst_mgr.lock - Wayne Lin
* Remove mentions of allowing multiple ACT updates per payload change
mention that this is a result of vendors not consistently supporting this
part of the spec and requiring a unique ACT for each payload change.
* Get rid of reference to drm_dp_mst_port in DC - turns out I just got
myself confused by DC and we don't actually need this.
Changes since v2:
* Get rid of fix for not sending payload deallocations if ddps=0 and just
go back to wayne's fix
